summary: 802.11w/MFP policy mismatch causes deauth storms and breaks zero-trust (WireGuard) reconnects in SF office
description:
Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-13 08:40 PST a subset of clients in the San Francisco office intermittently lose connectivity to internal services. Symptoms look like Wi‑Fi drops followed by failure to re-establish the WireGuard tunnel (zero-trust agent), which requires a manual restart of the agent to recover. Impact: ~12 users across two APs (floor 3) experienced repeated disconnects during the morning standup. Affected services: internal git, slack VPN-resolved flows, access to k8s API. Scope: office employees on macOS and Linux laptops using the corporate-ssid.

Impact: Internal productivity hit for on-site engineers; no customer-facing services affected. Outage window observed: 08:40–11:30 PST.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Connect company laptop to corporate-ssid at SF office APs SF-AP-23 / SF-AP-24.
2) Authenticate via 802.1X (Okta SAML -> RADIUS/EAP-TTLS).
3) Observe periodic deauths in system logs and zero-trust agent reporting 'interface down' and failing to resume WireGuard session.
4) Manual workaround: restart zero-trust agent or toggle Wi‑Fi to force reauth – this temporarily restores connectivity for the session.

Observed logs and evidence:
- AP syslog (SF-AP-23) around 08:43: "MFP policy mismatch: client RSN IE does not indicate MFP capability; rejecting management frame encryption negotiation; deauth/disassoc flood starting".
- wpa_supplicant (macOS/Linux) snippets: "supplicant: received deauth - reason 15, RSN: MFP required by AP but not supported by driver".
- Zero-trust agent (wireguard) logs: "wg0: interface went down due to link loss; handshake failed after reauth; route table entries flushed".
- Packet capture near AP: retransmitted deauth/disassoc frames, RSN IE mismatch visible in beacon and association response frames.
- AP controller shows recent configuration push at 03:00 UTC: SSID 'corporate-ssid' MFP policy set to 'required' as part of a security hardening roll (change-id cf-2026-03-13-03).

Initial hypothesis: Recent wireless baseline hardening set 802.11w (Management Frame Protection) to 'required' for corporate-ssid; some clients/drivers (older macOS kernel modules, older Linux Wi-Fi drivers, and our zero-trust onboarding images) do not advertise MFP capability properly leading to association but failing protected management frame negotiation, resulting in frequent deauths. When the client temporarily rejoins, the zero-trust agent's interface down event causes routing flush which WireGuard's automatic handshake does not recover from until agent restart.
investigation_notes:
Timeline:
- 08:45: CSI alerted from #internal-it Slack about multiple disconnected users on floor 3.
- 09:00: Collected AP syslogs and client logs from affected users (macOS 12.6.7 and Ubuntu 22.04 kernels). Observed consistent RSN IE differences.
- 09:20: Correlated with a controller change: config push cf-2026-03-13-03 set 'MFP: required' on corporate-ssid. This was part of a security sprint (PR: github.com/redwood/infra-config/pull/512).
- 09:35: Reproduced locally with a test Linux laptop: toggling MFP policy on AP between 'required' and 'optional' changed client behavior; 'required' triggered deauth storms on certain drivers.
- 10:10: Confirmed that zero-trust agent (wireguard) does not always gracefully recover route entries after multiple rapid link flaps; handshake stalls and session keys are not re-established until agent restart.

Hypotheses tested:
- MFP requirement causes client not to support protected management frames -> repeated deauths. Supported by packet captures and client RSN IE.
- Zero-trust agent's reconnection logic does not handle rapid link churn -> requires manual restart. Reproduced by simulated flaps.

Mitigation attempts:
- Temporarily set MFP policy to 'optional' for SF AP group (SF-AP-23/24) at 10:50 to stop deauth storms. Immediate decrease in incidents observed.
- Eng SRE pushed zero-trust agent update to improve reconnect logic (edge fix) on a test host but full rollout postponed pending QA.
comments: Priya Raman (Reporter) 2026-03-13 09:02: Noticed 3-4 folks on floor 3 reporting repeated disconnects. Collected client logs. Adding AP controller team.
Janelle (Network Eng) 2026-03-13 09:18: Found recent config change cf-2026-03-13-03 setting MFP required. Rolling back MFP to optional for SF AP group to test impact.
Liam O'Connor (Assignee) 2026-03-13 10:55: Rolled MFP to optional for SF-AP-23/24. Immediate drop in deauth events. Will monitor for 2 hours.

SRE (Marco) 2026-03-13 11:30: Observed wireguard hang reproduction on test host after repeated link flaps. Created stub PR to add a hard restart/backoff in reconnect logic (github.com/redwood/wireguard-agent/pull/78).

Liam O'Connor 2026-03-14 09:15: Confirmed rollout plan: AP controller firmware/config baseline to set MFP to 'optional' until client fleet updated. Scheduled agent rollouts for next week. Marking Incident resolved after config change and monitoring window.
Security (Priya K) 2026-03-14 12:04: Noted that MFP requirement was a security hardening ask. Approving temporary relaxation with plan to re-enable once clients updated and agent fix shipped.
resolution: Temporary rollback: MFP policy changed from 'required' -> 'optional' on SF AP group (SF-AP-23/24) at 2026-03-13 10:50 PST which stopped deauth storm. Long-term fix: (1) Deploy zero-trust agent update v2.8.0 with improved reconnect/backoff and MFP capability reporting (PR #78) – rollout planned 2026-03-17. (2) Push AP firmware 7.2.1 and updated controller profile that allows 'optional' MFP with compatibility mode and clear rollout tests. Change window for re-enablement of 'required' MFP will be scheduled after fleet verification. Incident closed after 24h stable monitoring on 2026-03-14.
follow_up_actions: Roll out wireguard-agent v2.8.0 to all endpoint images (tracking: infra-deploy ticket INT-935102)
AP controller firmware update to 7.2.1 and new SSID profile that negotiates MFP compat mode (change request CR-2026-03-20)
Add monitoring alert: spike in deauth/disassoc events per AP -> auto-create incident (alerts #net-deauth-spike)
Document compatibility matrix for MFP in internal runbook (confluence: /network/runbooks/mfp-compatibility)
Security review to sign off on re-enabling 'required' MFP once 95% of endpoints have updated agent/driver support
